children: The National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) has declared September 7 as the appointed date for the Agra-Gwalior Greenfield Road project, G R Infraprojects announced on September 18.

The "Construction of Agra-Gwalior Greenfield Road" project comprises two sections. The first section involves development of a six-lane, access-controlled Agra-Gwalior greenfield highway, starting near village Deori in Agra district and extending 88.4 kilometres to a point near village Susera in Gwalior district, spanning Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh.

The second section covers road safety improvements and resurfacing along a 90-kilometre stretch of the existing Agra-Gwalior highway (NH-44), spanning across Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh

Estimated at ₹4,262.78 crore inclusive of GST, the project will be executed under the government's National Highways (Original) scheme. It is structured as a public-private partnership using the Design-Build-Finance-Operate-Transfer (DBFOT) pattern under the BOT (Toll) mode. Under this agreement, the private developer will entirely fund, construct, and maintain the highway, recovering its investment by collecting commuter tolls for a specified period before transferring ownership back to NHAI. The project has a construction timeline of 910 days (approximately 2.5 years) from the officially declared appointed start date.
Shares of G R Infraprojects Limited closed at ₹823.40 on the NSE on September 18, 2026, down ₹5.65 or 0.68%. The stock has fallen over 17% in the year so far.

title: G R Infra gets appointed date from NHAI for ₹4,263 crore Agra-Gwalior highway project
